sections.content:
In sequal to ECON3800: extending your research proposal in 3800 into a journal-length (50 pages) thesis. The length may sound freaky at first, but the recommended typesetting is 12pt font, double-space, one-inch margin with figures and references included. So it's actually very easy to achieve. However, as a document formatting OCDer, I used more compact linespace and smaller margins, and ended up with 68 pages.

WARNING: If you are considering doing SBMT4000 under an economics professor, please spend a minute reading my friend's review: https://ust.space/review/SBMT4000
sections.teaching:
Actually four instructors:
Prof. Pak Hung AU: HT supervisor
Prof. Jenny XU: My (designated) thesis reviewer
Prof. Jiaming HUANG: My (selected by Pak Hung) thesis reviewer
Prof. Byoungchan LEE: My thesis supervisor

I did my ECON4800 during exchange at University of Notre Dame. Prof. Lee was traveling between Seoul and Hong Kong during Fall 2025, so we should zoom anyway whether or not I am off to exchange.

We had an 13-14 hour time lag, but he is always very very very responsive. Emails will be replied within 24 hours (typically 15-18 hours). Sometimes I received his emails in afternoons (2-3 P.M.) ~ 2-4 a.m. in HK or Seoul. He was traveling between academic conferences in both cities, his Ph.D. Qichao was in job market, plus what he always joked with his students that being a father (family man) of a 3-4 year-old boy isn't easy enough (becuz the boy is quiet in the mornings but crys in sleeping hours). So I would affirm he did his BEST as a thesis supervisor to an undergrad. He could pay less attention to me (becuz supervising an undergrad is definitely NOT his KPI) though, but he replied concrete and informatively to most of my questions. Sometimes receiving a long email in the morning is... quiet conventional. Thank to him.

We shared a Overleaf for thesis and presentation slides. I captured him reviewing my once. Upon pointing out inconsistenticies and non-rigorosities, he even modified my grammers, spelling (typo I think) and punctuation marks (I missed with all inline equations and he added all manually). He was actually reading my thesis word-by-word...

Futhermore, he provided the BEST emotional values. He always says it's  (VAR-typeshit) already very hard for undergrad and you are doing a great job (although sometimes with nasty results).  I went through a hard time during Thanksgiving (personal issues) just before the Thesis presentation. He attended my presentation via Zoom and helped me out in a tricky question by Pak Hung. After that I sent him a email of gratitude, and he replied something I will never forget in my life:

"The outcome is definitely better than what I could have done myself when I was an undergraduate student years ago."

I am crystal clear he is self-humbling again. Receiving Ph.D. offers from UC Berkeley, Uchicago and Minnsota right after undergrad is certainly NOT what I can do. But it was this sentence that pulled me out of the emotional slump I had been in for a long time.

Certainly our interaction is now beyond the thesis that I am willing to audit his Quant Macroeconomics (Similar to ECON60202: Macro II at Univ of Notre Dame) in my final semester at HKUST. Spending a year interacting and collaborating with an angel-like professor, and later finding opportunities to share some heartfelt words with him, is quite rare for an undergraduate student. Just like how I acknowledged him at my end of the presentation: "Prof Lee is one of the best teachers I've ever met in my life..."

Both Prof. Huang and Xu wrote me lengthy feedbacks. They always pinpoint some major issues in other aspects and, after addressing them, can indeed elevate the rigor and accuracy to new heights. Meanwhile they are also very responsive. You can ask them about anything you don't understand in their comments, and they will resolve your confusion with great patience.

Prof AU: Great and very thoughful coordination with on-time updates.

In short: HKUST ECON Department is the goat of the biz-school.
sections.grading:
A+

The grade is based on your supervisor and other thesis committee members, who are formed by Prof. Au. There are no clear rubrics (unlike SBMT4000), and the Professors are supportive. So a lenient grading could be expected from the beginning.

Based on my observation, the baseline is A-, determined by completeness and attitude. An A-range is secured as long as you submit a proper and completed thesis. A and A+ will be determined largely on your methodology and synthesis quality.

However, attitude accounts for the most. Make sure you are always serious about this work, that's the utmost thing professors want you to show. Show them how you (attempted to) fix a problem through the regular meetings and always exchange your ideas and adopt their advice. At least, I haven't seen anyone with a grade lower than A-.
sections.workload:
OrtI spent the time nearly tantamount to my Ph.D. Macro in Notre Dame: ECON 60201 (The hardest and creazist course ever taken)

Awful and brutal. It can be exceptionally large if you enjoy wrestling with yourself (like me). To minimize your workload, do these things:
RULE OF THUMB: Check out how to properly preprocess and normalize your data based on your model beforehand. THIS IS CRUCIAL.

1. Start in the spring semester, and spend the summer working on it as well. If you start in the fall, spare all the winter for it. The leftover time in the subsequent semester is terse.
2. Find existing replication package in relevant literatures.
3. Contact your supervisor anytime you get stuck or find something intriguing.
4. NEVER EVER PILE THINGS UP!!!
5. Never give up! You will survive. Everyone is very very supportive
6. Don't take other crazy courses during ECON4800. 3800 is fine.
7. A research fund of pp HKD 3000 is available for purchasing data and software. Apply if needed!
8. Compromise when it's time to do so, and leave some room for your future self. Don't overstruggle on a certain point. You are just an undergrad, don't expect too much (Otherwise, Ph.D. programs will be meaningless) Being able to write down a single-author journal-length thesis is already HARD enough and it is a GREAT POSITIVE SIGNAL in your application.

Good Luck!
